title: Meccha Chameleon
genre: Online multiplayer hide-and-seek / prop-hunt variant (players paint themselves to blend into the environment)
developer: Lemorion_1224 and Haganeiro (two Japanese developers) [per brief, unverified]
developer_background: The two developers met in the Fortnite custom-map (UEFN/Creative) community [per brief, unverified]. Previous released games: no data.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (appid not retrieved – no data). Other platforms: no data.
business_model: Premium, ~$5.99 [per brief]; one source in the brief says $4.79 at launch, which is consistent with a 20% launch discount on $5.99 (inference). No advertising spend [dev claim per brief].
price_usd: ~$5.99 list; possibly $4.79 at launch (-20%) [per brief, unverified]
units_or_downloads: 10,000,000 copies by 2026-06-26 and 15,000,000 in under a month (i.e. by ~early July 2026) [CONFIRMED-claimed – developer claims as cited in the research brief; NOT re-verified this session]. Current total (Oct 2026): no data.
peak_concurrent_players: ~340,534 on 2026-06-21 [per brief, likely SteamDB; NOT re-verified]
gross_revenue: ≈ $67M by ~early Jul 2026 [ESTIMATE – spec method: 15M units × ($5.99 × 0.75 = $4.49); input units are unverified dev claims]. If regional pricing (a large Asian audience is likely but unverified) pulled the average realised price down to ~$3.50, gross ≈ $52M. Range $50M–$70M. No tracker estimate retrieved.
net_revenue: ≈ $47M [ESTIMATE] = $67.4M gross − Steam cut (30% on first $10M = $3.0M; 25% on $10M–$50M = $10.0M; 20% on $50M–$67.4M = $3.5M) = $50.9M × 0.93 ≈ $47.3M. Publisher/split: no data.
production_cost: ≈ $24k [ESTIMATE – 2 people × ~2 months × $6k/month (Japan lean indie)]. No disclosed figure. No ad spend (dev claim per brief).
why_popular: Hide-and-seek in which you paint yourself to match the scenery. The hook is instantly understandable, very clip-able (the 'where is he?' reveal moment), works as a social party game with friends, and is cheap (~$6). [qualitative, based on the brief's description]
marketing_channels: No paid advertising [dev claim per brief]. Other channels (streamers, TikTok/Shorts clips, Japanese/Asian streamers, Next Fest): no data – not searched.
engine: no data. Speculation only: the founders' UEFN/Fortnite background might suggest Unreal Engine, but this is unverified.
art_style: no data (likely bright, simple 3D given the 2-month build; unverified)
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the core loop (seeker/hider rounds, timer, scoring), the colour-sampling and self-paint shader logic, lobby code, and generate simple 3D environments/props, SFX and music. | AI cannot: tune the hide/seek balance (how close a paint match must be, map readability, round length), make the paint mechanic feel satisfying, run playtests with real groups, or create the viral spark. Syncing a per-player paint texture over the network needs care but is moderate. The original 2-person team reportedly built it in ~2 months. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 or Godot 4 (or UE5) + Steam lobbies (Facepunch.Steamworks/GodotSteam) + Meshy/Tripo or asset packs for environments + ElevenLabs SFX + Suno music.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, ~$200–$600 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$200/mo, 3D gen $20–$60/mo, asset packs $50–$200, Steam Direct $100). Excludes living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months, ~$1,500–$5,000 (tools, asset packs, freelance trailer/key art, playtest and creator outreach). Excludes living costs.
